title: Personal Assistant - Immediate Start
description:
Personal Assistant

Location: Brighton
Hours: Monday-Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm
Working Pattern: Full time 3-4 days per week in the office 1 from home

Salary: 15 - 17 (DOE)

The Role

We are looking for a highly organised and proactive Personal Assistant to provide dedicated support to two senior stakeholders. This role is ideal for an experienced PA who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys managing multiple priorities, and has strong technical and systems skills.

You will be responsible for ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of schedules, meetings, documentation, and administrative processes, whilst maintaining a high level of accuracy and professionalism.

Key Responsibilities
- Complex diary management and scheduling for two senior team members
- Organising meetings, preparing agendas, and coordinating logistics
- Producing and distributing meeting minutes with quick turnaround times
- Managing, maintaining, and organising documentation across SharePoint and internal systems
- Ensuring document accuracy, version control, and effective file management
- Creating and formatting professional documents, reports, and presentations
- Supporting with spreadsheet management, reporting, and data administration using Excel
- Acting as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders
- Providing general administrative and organisational support as required

Key Requirements
- Previous experience in a Personal Assistant, Executive Assistant, or Senior Administrator role
- Excellent diary management and scheduling skills
- Strong systems capability with confidence using Microsoft Office applications
- Advanced working knowledge of SharePoint, Microsoft Word, Outlook, and Excel
- Experience managing document libraries and maintaining document version control
- Ability to produce accurate meeting minutes and notes within tight deadlines
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise competing demands
- High attention to detail and strong document management skills
- Professional communication skills and the ability to build effective working relationships
- Proactive, adaptable, and able to work independently

What We're Looking For

The successful candidate will be a confident administrator with exceptional attention to detail, strong technical skills, and the ability to keep processes organised and running efficiently. You will enjoy supporting senior stakeholders, managing confidential information, and ensuring documents and communications are maintained to a high standard.

If you are a highly organised PA with strong systems knowledge and the ability to deliver in a fast-paced environment, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Childrens Support Worker
description:
Childrens Support Worker - Worthing - April 2026

Are you looking for your first step on the ladder to progress into teaching or a therapy-focused role?

Perhaps you are an experienced childrens support worker and you're looking for a new setting?

A well established school for children aged 11-18 with ADHD and/or Autism are welcoming applicants who are able to demonstrate a good academic background, along with the characteristics of resilience, empathy, creativity and problem-solving. - Excellent training and development opportunities within the school
- Term time working hours
- Excellent experience to further your career

- Helping the children with completing academic tasks

- Liaising with other staff members across the therapy and senior leadership teams

- A DBS check (we can support you with an application for one)
- A minimum of grade A -C in GCSE Maths and English

Apply for this Childrens Support Worker role today or get in touch with Academics Crawley for more info.

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker Eastbourne (Agency / Ad Hoc Shifts)-WE DO NOT OFFER SPONSORSHIP

Location: Eastbourne, East Sussex
Pay Rate: £12.71 per hour
Job Type: Agency / Temporary
Hours: Flexible Ad Hoc Shifts (Days, Nights, Weekends & Bank Holidays Available)

About the Role

AA Euro Healthcare is currently recruiting Support Workers to join a leading national social care provider supporting adults with learning disabilities, autism, mental health needs, and complex support requirements across services in Eastbourne.

This is an excellent opportunity for caring and dedicated individuals seeking flexible agency work, allowing them to choose shifts that fit around their existing commitments while making a meaningful difference to people's lives.

Key Responsibilities
- Delivering person-centred support that promotes independence and wellbeing.
- Assisting individuals with daily living activities and personal care where required.
- Supporting service users to participate in community activities, hobbies, and appointments.
- Encouraging choice, dignity, inclusion, and self-determination.
- Assisting with medication administration in line with service procedures.
- Maintaining accurate records and completing relevant documentation.
- Identifying and reporting safeguarding concerns appropriately.
- Building positive and professional relationships with service users, families, and multidisciplinary teams.

Requirements
- Previous experience within health and social care is desirable but not essential.
- A compassionate and person-centred approach to support.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
- Reliability, flexibility, and a positive attitude.
- Enhanced DBS on the Update Service is advantageous (or willingness to obtain one).
- Right to work in the UK.

What We Offer
- Flexible ad hoc agency shifts.
- Weekly pay.
- Ongoing support from a dedicated healthcare recruitment consultant.
- Opportunities to gain experience across a variety of support settings.
- Access to additional shifts and future assignments.

Why Join?

This role offers the chance to work with a highly respected care organisation that is committed to empowering people to live the lives they choose. You will be supporting individuals to develop skills, achieve personal goals, and actively engage within their local community.

Apply Today

If you are a caring, dependable, and motivated Support Worker looking for flexible agency opportunities in Eastbourne, we would love to hear from you.

AA Euro Healthcare is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of vulnerable adults. All successful applicants will be subject to satisfactory references, enhanced DBS clearance, and right-to-work checks.

title: Childrens Support Worker - Weekends
description:
Children's Support Worker - Weekends

Join Nurse Plus as a Children's Support Worker - Make a difference everday

At Nurseplus, every shift you work is an opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of those in need. As a temporary Support Worker, you ll be providing high-quality care across a range of settings, from elderly care to individuals with learning disabilities, mental health challenges, and more complex care needs. You ll become part of a compassionate team where every contribution counts.

Why Choose Nurseplus?
- Weekly Pay & Competitive Rates: Earn from £16.00 per hour paid weekly, depending on shift pattern (higher rates apply for nights, weekends, and bank holidays).
- Workwise App: Take control of your schedule with our Workwise app manage your availability and easily book shifts on your terms.
- Paid Industry-Leading Training: We pay for you to attend our comprehensive, industry-leading training that s in line with the Care Certificate and Core Skills Training Framework, tailored to help you grow your skills, whether you re new to care or have years of experience.
- Ongoing Development Opportunities: From in-house courses to funded qualifications such as NVQ Levels 2 and 3, we support your professional growth at every stage.
- Blue Light Card: Enjoy thousands of discounts on the high street and online with eligibility for a Blue Light Card.

What You ll Be Doing

Your day-to-day responsibilities as a Support Worker may include assisting service users with personal care, safe lifting and moving, administering medication, meal preparation, and providing general companionship. You ll work closely with care plans to ensure individuals maintain independence and dignity, providing the physical and emotional support that they might need to achieve their goals.

What We re Looking For
- You must be over 18 years old and have the right to work in the UK.
- Flexibility in your availability, with weekend and afternoon/evening availability
- A good standard of English and the ability to communicate effectively.
- A clear enhanced DBS, which you can apply for upon registration.
- A full UK driving licence is essential, and we cover full travel expenses up to 45p per mile.

If you re passionate about making a positive impact and want to work with a team that truly cares, we d love to hear from you!

About Nurseplus

At Nurseplus, our mission is to make a positive impact and change lives every day. We are passionate about delivering the highest-quality care that truly makes a difference in the lives of those we support. But our commitment doesn t stop there we care just as much for our staff as we do for our clients. By fostering a supportive and inclusive environment, we empower our team to grow, thrive, and make a meaningful contribution to the communities they serve.

title: Residential Support Worker - Ofsted Registered Children's Home
description:
Residential Support Worker - Ofsted Registered Children's Residential Home

Job Title: Residential Support Worker

Pay: 13.82 - 17.29 per hour

Location: Eastbourne

Working Pattern: Day or Night Shifts Available

In this role you will help young people become more independent and grow personally through various enjoyable activities within a safe environment. This is a truly rewarding opportunity where you have a fulfilling chance to positively influence the lives of vulnerable children and young people who have experienced trauma, instability and adversity.

As a Residential Support Worker, you will play a vital role in creating a therapeutic, nurturing and structured environment where young people feel understood, supported and cared for within a Ofsted Registered Children's Home in Eastbourne, which is rated "Good".

The home is a specialist residential children's home supporting up to 4 young people aged 13 to 17 (currently supporting one young person) with complex and additional needs, including foetal alcohol syndrome, learning disabilities, ADHD, sensory processing difficulties, visual impairment, developmental delays and communication difficulties.

The role requires individuals who can remain calm, patient and resilient when supporting behaviours that may challenge, including verbal and physical aggression, property damage and self injurious behaviours. You will work closely with colleagues to follow individual care plans, risk assessments and positive behaviour support strategies. Personal care is also an important part of this role, including supporting personal hygiene, bathing, dressing and continence needs where required, while promoting independence, dignity and choice.

We are looking for compassionate, active and emotionally intelligent individuals who can combine warmth and relationship building with professional boundaries, consistency and a genuine commitment to improving a young person's quality of life.

What We Offer:
- Exceptional Hourly Rates, 13.82 - 17.29 Per Hour
- Private Healthcare and 24/7 GP Access with Vitality
- Fully Funded Level 3 and Level 5 Qualifications
- Clear Career Pathways with Higher Salaries
- Excellent Work Life Balance
- 40 per month Gym Membership Contributions / Fitness Classes
- Enhanced Maternity / Paternity / Adoption Packages
- Free Access to Flexible and Unlimited Therapeutic Support
- Birthday Paid Off
- Free or Subsidised Parking
- Enhanced Overtime Rates
- Company Bonus Scheme
- Free Meals on Every Shift including Snacks and Refreshments in Offices
- Blue Light Card Membership Included
- Company Sick Pay Policy (Above Statutory)
- Pension Scheme
- Frequent Company Events

About You:
- Experience working with children or young people (preferred)
- A genuine passion for supporting vulnerable young people
- Strong communication and relationship building skills
- Emotional resilience and the ability to remain calm under pressure
- The ability to work within professional boundaries
- A trauma informed and child centred approach
- Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare (preferred) or willingness to complete

Key Responsibilities:

As a Residential Support Worker you will:
- Provide safe, consistent and therapeutic care to children and young people
- Support the emotional, physical and psychological wellbeing of young people
- Build positive, professional and consistent relationships while maintaining clear boundaries
- Safeguard and promote welfare in line with legislation, Local Authority guidance and organisational policies
- Deliver care in line with therapeutic models, PBS plans and individual care plans
- Support young people to regulate emotions and develop appropriate behaviours
- Promote independence, life skills and engagement in education and routines
- Contribute to meaningful activities, trips and experiences for young people
- Work collaboratively as part of a high performing residential team
- Maintain accurate records, daily logs and incident reports
- Contribute to handovers, team meetings and reflective practice
- Support the maintenance of a safe, clean and homely environment
- Administer medication in line with training and policy
- Work flexibly across different homes within the service where required

Working Hours & Shift Patterns:

This home operates a 24 hour, 365 day service. You have the choice of working Day Shifts or Night Shifts. The shift patterns are as follows:

Day Shifts
- 1 day on, 2 days off (rolling rota)
- 07:30am - 10:30pm (15 hour shifts)

Waking Night Shifts
- 2 nights on, 2 nights off (rolling rota)
- 10:00pm - 08:00am (10 hour shifts)

Safer Recruitment

All roles are subject to Enhanced DBS checks, referencing and full safer recruitment procedures.

If you are passionate about supporting children and young people to achieve positive outcomes and want to join a provider committed to outstanding care, apply now to become part of the team!

title: Night Care Assistant - Bank
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Care Assistant at a Barchester care home, you'll help residents enjoy each day by making sure they get the quality care and support they deserve. You'll assist with daily living, providing support and companionship and sharing great moments and memories too. It's a chance to bring your dedication and compassion to a fulfilling environment. Every day will be different, so you can expect to undertake work that's as varied as it is rewarding. As a Care Assistant, you could be doing anything from supporting residents with their food and drink and following care plans to ensuring that each of our residents has one-to-one time. It's an opportunity to put your skills to meaningful use and develop your career.

ABOUT YOU
To join us as a Care Assistant you'll need to have some experience of caring for older people, a can-do approach and excellent communication skills. Your empathy and warm-hearted approach will shine through, but above all, you'll have the compassion needed to deliver the highest standard of care and support for all our residents. In return we'll provide all the training you need to thrive.

REWARDS PACKAGE
In return for your dedication, you'll receive a competitive rate of pay plus our sector-leading benefits and rewards package including:
Free training and development for all roles
Access to wellbeing and support tools
A range of retail discounts and savings
Unlimited referrals with our Refer a Friend' bonus scheme
Employee of the Month' rewards and Long Service Awards'

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality care you'd expect for your loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

title: Behaviour Support Assistant
description:
Behaviour Support Assistant

Crawley - West Sussex - Education - Mental health - SEN - SEMH - MLD - 93-105

Are you wanting to make a difference for children and young people with Special Needs?

This specialist secondary school in Crawley is looking for a dedicated Behaviour Support Assistant to join the team. The setting caters for young people who have Social, Emotional and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, and Moderate Learning Difficulties (MLD), and/or Autism Spectrum conditions. These pupils may have experienced disrupted education, school refusal, anxiety or exclusion, find mainstream setting overwhelming, need small groups, high adult consistency and trusted relationships to succeed.

A Behaviour Support Assistant is a great way to kick start your career within the SEN sector. With this role in Crawley, you will have the chance to work closely aside and network with a range of professionals, such as, Therapists and Counsellors. This is an amazing opportunity to get your 'foot in the door', whilst gaining first-hand experience and expanding your knowledge and skillsets. If you are looking for career progression routes that include SEN Teacher, Youth Worker, Social Worker, Counsellor, Educational Psychologist, and many more, then this Behaviour Support Assistant in Crawley is for you!

Job role and responsibilities for a Behaviour Support Assistant:
- Assist the class teacher with the learning experience
- Provide dedicated support to pupils with learning, physical, sensory, or behavioural challenges
- Ability to build trusted and effective relationships with the pupils
- Willing to do 1:1 and small group support and work with pupils
- Follow the safeguarding guidelines and implement them in the classroom
- Have good communication and interpersonal skills
- Be a good listener with a compassionate and caring approach
- Needs to attend staff meetings and complete relevant CPD
- Able to commute to Crawley

Start date October or ASAP, trial days taking place to ensure the role and school is right for you
Fantastic on-site training, support and CPD is provided to ensure safeguarding of all pupils
Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 15:30, PAYE, term time only
93- 105 per day
You MUST have right to work in the UK in order to apply - no Visa sponsorship
- Candidates registering with Academics will need to have or apply for an Enhanced DBS and/or overseas police check where appropriate

Apply now or contact Maddy Thatcher at Academics if interested in the role:
(phone number removed) l (url removed)

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.
